title: Make a Positive Array
summary: Given an array nums, determine the least number of operations required to make it positive.
statement: Given an array nums, determine the least number of operations required to make it positive. An array is positive if every subarray with more than two elements has a positive sum. An operation consists of replacing any single element in nums with an integer between -10^18 and 10^18.
constraints: A positive array has strictly positive sum for every contiguous subarray of length at least three.
One operation may replace one element by any integer from -10^18 to 10^18; minimize replacements.
hints: Replacing one selected position by a huge positive value fixes every bad subarray containing it, reducing the task to stabbing all non-positive intervals of length at least three.
Scan by right endpoint and greedily replace the current right endpoint as soon as any uncovered bad interval appears.
Track the prefix sum and largest eligible earlier prefix since the last replacement; reset both after selecting an endpoint.
Earliest-ending interval stabbing is optimal: any solution must hit the detected interval, and moving that hit to its right endpoint cannot hurt a later interval.
editorial: Earliest-ending interval stabbing is optimal: any solution must hit the detected interval, and moving that hit to its right endpoint cannot hurt a later interval.

tests.explanation: The only length-three subarray sums to -7, and replacing one of its entries is sufficient.
All non-positive long subarrays share an early position, so one replacement fixes them.
